sections.skill: Measure whether a tool is worth its cost

questions.domain: Foundation 12: AI as a practical helper
questions.prompt: Which is a cost of a tool besides its price?

choices.text: Time spent learning and checking its work
The number of its employees worldwide

questions.correct_answer: Time spent learning and checking its work
questions.intro: A tool is worth using only if it helps. MEASURE the benefit: time saved, errors reduced, or sales gained, compared with the cost (subscription price plus time spent learning and checking). Example: a 20-dollar-a-month tool that saves 3 hours a month is worth it if your time is worth more than about 6.67 dollars an hour. Try a tool on one task first, compare before and after, and drop tools that do not help. Check terms, data handling and whether you can export your work.

questions.domain: Foundation 12: AI as a practical helper
questions.prompt: 20 dollars a month saves 4 hours. What is the cost per hour saved?
questions.intro: To judge a tool, divide its monthly cost by the hours it saves each month. Example: 24 dollars / 4 hours saved = 6 dollars per hour saved. If your time is worth more than that per hour, the tool pays off. Include checking time: if the tool saves 4 hours but checking takes 1 hour, the net saving is 3 hours, so 24 / 3 = 8 dollars per hour saved.
